items.title: 67848_Jimmy McPartland oral history interview
items.q: Jack Donahue and Lily Damita (Louis Damita?) on Broadway. So, Benny Goodman said, well get Jimmy McPartland.

ctx.x: Rubinoff needed a clarinet player, a saxophone player and I called, well I was living, Benny and I were living together what am I talking about. So I told Benny about it and he went over and he got the job. And the same thing happened with me. Mannie Klein the trumpet player was talking to Benny Goodman about he didn't want to take a job with a show called, 'Sons of Guns'. Jack Donahue and Lily Damita (Louis Damita?) on Broadway.

So, Benny Goodman said, well get Jimmy McPartland. He plays second trumpet and plays jazz, hot, you know, they call it hot cornet you know, hot. Playing hot in those days we would call it. Can you play hot? You know, jazz. Hot jazz. So I went over and auditioned for the job and I got the job in 'Sons of Guns'.
